messages:
Amanda: FYI nightly eval drift alert — hallucination rate jumped on qa_corebench_v2 after deploy of model rdm/v5.2 + tokenizer merge

Eval-bot: nightly eval report: model: rdm/v5.2; eval_set: qa_corebench_v2; HR (threshold 0.7): baseline 3.2% -> 12.8% (+9.6pp); EM drop: 87.1 -> 74.3; avg gen len +18%

Kai: tagging — did we change tokenizer in same PR? @Jorge

Jorge: yep, tokenizer merge + new merges file landed in commits abc123 / def456 yesterday. weights were recompiled after that. suspect tokenization shift.

Amanda: repro steps i ran:
```
# run single prompt from failing set
python eval/run_gen.py --model rdm/v5.2 --prompts data/qa_corebench_v2/fails.txt --seed 42
```
output: several answers start with 'In 2023' when ground truth is 2019. hallucinations referencing events not in context.

Maria: i pulled a pairwise comparison of tokenization between v5.1 weights + old tokenizer and v5.2 + new tokenizer:
```
avg_tokens_old: 12.3
avg_tokens_new: 10.1
out_of_vocab_new_tokens: 0.6% -> 2.1%
notable merges: 'San' + ' ' + 'Francisco' -> 'SanFrancisco' (new)
```

Kai: that compression could shift attention positions and kv cache alignment — if the model was trained with old segmentation, new merges can change positional dynamics.

Jorge: also saw a change in bos/eos ids in the new tokenizer mapping (bos id moved 1 slot). Could break some postprocessing heuristics.

Amanda: i can confirm reproduces on a local dedicated GPU with v5.2 weights + new tokenizer. with v5.2 weights + old tokenizer the HR is 4.1% so weights alone unlikely.

Jorge: plan: (1) run a bisect on tokenizer commit range (abc100..def456) using the nightly harness, (2) run eval with new tokenizer + old mapping of special tokens (remap ids) as an experiment, (3) revert tokenizer merge on staging and run A/B.

Kai: i'll start the bisect job on ci-nightly. tagging @eval-bot to create a compare run.

Eval-bot: created job id 2026-03-20-1205-compare-tokenizer-abc100-def456 across qa_corebench_v2. will post results here when done.

Amanda: also flagging this to product (sla risk) and ops if we need to rollback hosted model exposures. @sre-bot please hold any scheduled promotion of rdm/v5.2 to prod until we resolve.

sre-bot: acknowledged — hold on promos set.

Maria: quick note — i found one failing prompt where new tokenization glued a prefix 'no-' into a token leading to negation loss. example:
```
prompt: 'Is it safe?'
gold: 'No, because...'
new gen: 'Yes, it is safe.'
```

Jorge: good catch. that explains flips on yes/no where prefixes changed.

Amanda: ok summary: suspected root cause = tokenizer merge changing subword boundaries + special token id shifts. immediate mitigation = remap special ids and run bisect; if confirmed rollback tokenizer. i'll own the remediation. assigning @Jorge to run tokenizer remap experiment, @Kai to monitor bisect.

Kai: noted. i'll update this thread with first bisect result (~2h).

Amanda: thanks team :thumbsup:
